Comrade General, Your Tank Army must as soon as possible cross the Vistula river and establish a bridgehead on its western bank. We expect very strong German resistance.
Za Swabodu!!! - For the Freedom!!! (ZS#14), 06/01/1945
Comrade Marshal, we've beaten these Nazi pigs, but their capitalistic allies still endanger our Motherland and tyrannize the Europe's working class! We still must fight for their liberation!
Comrade Stalin has ordered you to destroy with sudden assault the forces of capitalist-fascist US' regime in middle Germany - then you'll liberate the Rühr and march towards Paris!
Prusy Wschodnie - East Prussia (ZS#10), 08/20/1944

Comrade General, your Tank Army is temporarily commanded to the Baltic Front. With a sudden strike we should capture East Prussia and thus leave the Germans with no possibility of counterattacking our troops on the Vistula's western bank. Tell your soldiers they have the honour of bringing the war into the German territory - you have to rape, burn, murder and plunder. Let these fascist scums feel the war!!!

Wacht am Rhein - December 20th, 1944

Lines have stabilized after your retreat from Normandy. Hitler has gathered all available forces for a counterattack. Your division and the 9thSS Hohenstaufen form the 2SS Pz Corps. The original plan called for you to exploit the initial success of the 1SS Pz Corps attack on the northern shoulder of our attack through the Ardennes. The enemy however has stalled the LSSAH's attack. The goal of advancing as far west as Antwerp and cutting the Allied forces in half has been given up.

Your troops have been transferred from 6SSPz Armee to the 5PzArmee and have swung south around LSSAH. Your task is to capture the crossroads at Baraque Fraiture, push through the US lines of defense and capture Liege. Maybe that will move the Allies to start peace negotiations.
Smolensk-Crossing the Dniepr - July 7th, 1941

Guderian has decided to not wait for the infantry divisions and to cross the Dniepr with only his mobile troops because General Hoth's 3rd Panzer Gruppe has already done the same to the north of us. Both Gruppen could meet at Smolensk thereby trapping more Russians in a new pocket. 10Pz Division will cross the Dniepr North of Mogilev with your division and the GrossDeutschland Infantry Regiment covering the flanks. The first goals are Kopyr and Gorki.

You are to make contact with von Kleist's 1 Pz Gruppe South of Konotop to complete the encirclement. The capture of Moscow will have to wait. Opposing your forces is the newly created Russian 40th Army assisted by the 2nd Air-landing Corps and the 10th Tank Division.

Operation Typhoon - Moscow - November 24th, 1941

We had to break up our 11SS Regiment to bring the Deutschland and Der Fürher regiments up to strength again. Some of our units have started to run out of ammo. But even though the  mud, rain and cold slowed us down, we have come close to the end goal of our offensive: the capture of Moscow. The 10th Pz Division will again be fighting at our left flank. Make us proud General.

Mission accomplished. The retreat was safe and our forces are almost intact.

Model's 9th Army in the North and Kempf's III Panzer Corps on our right flank have not made much progress. Hoth's Fourth Panzer Army has done better and we are now in a position to capture Prokhorovka and extend the bridgehead over the Psel river west of Prokhorovka.
Totenkopf's bridgehead is under heavy attack by the Russian 1st Tank Army and the 5th Guards Tank Army is counterattacking out of the Prokhorovka direction to our East.

The story of 3 SS divisions attacking Prokhorovka with hundreds of Tiger and Panther tanks is a myth and so is the SS divisions loosing +400 tanks in the engagement. The Panther battalions were in Germany and each division had only 1 Tiger company. At the start of  Zitadelle, the 3 divisions of II SS Panzer Corps, totalled no more than about 350 tanks. By the time the battle for Prokhorovka started, the number of operational tanks had dropped to 211. Only 15 were Tigers. After the battle, II SS Panzer Corps reported 163 operational tanks. Russian tank losses were close to 650. Leibstandarte's 13th Tiger company (leader) was commanded by 2nd Lt. Michael Wittmann.

Now that we crossed the Dniepr and broken the Russian lines, the 10th Pz Division will move on Yelnya while your troops are ordered to capture Roslavl. Yelnya will be the starting point for our final drive on Moscow and Roslavl controls the main roads in this area.

After crossing the Ardenne Forest, your task is to strike the enemy at Sedan, where the Frenchs don't expect an attack. Drive your Panzer divisions to cross the Meuse River, and clear this sector, from Sedan to Rethel. Although we surely will surprise the Frenchs, they will sent at least one Army Corps as reinforcements. Exploit at the maximun the Blitzkrieg here, and show what we are capable of.
I should notice you, that due to the high number of units crossing the Ardenne forest, some Panzer units are still in the way, and will arrive in the next hours.

After this the Frenchs surely are completely scared!, we have destroyed their defenses in Sedan, and now we can launch our Panzer Divisions on to the heart of France. The enemy forces were waiting for us in the Low Countries, and now we will be able to trap them.
The Frenchs have stopped our main attack!, this is a complete disaster. Now our attack on the Low Countries is stopped, and we will face another trench war... like in 1914. You are dismissed.

I'm glad to inform you, that due to your outstanding achievement of the objectives, we have captured the enemy commander, the General Giraud.

The Soviets cross the Oder river and start a direct attack towards Berlin.

You and your men have won a rest for now!. The French resistance continues in some places, but the invasion of France is completed, and in the next days we will be celebrating the victory in the Champs Elysees in Paris!!. Personally, I think that the pause made in the final assault on Duenkirchen, will cause consequences in the future...

After a day of heavy fighting the Leibstandarte seized the Klidi Pass.  The British immediately began to withdraw to a defensive line west of Mount Olympus and the Greek 1st Army began to pull out of Albania.

The brigade recon battalion, commanded by Kurt 'Panzer' Meyer was then odered to advance further through the Klissura Pass and on to Lake Kastoria.  One of the most infamous incidents of the SS is recorded from this assault.  Finding his soldiers pinned down by enemy fire and unwilling to attack, Meyer decided to toss a grenade at his own soldiers.  The effect was immediate, the soldiers picked themselves up and wrested control of the enemy positions from the ANZAC defenders.

Despite initial successes of Polish and Canadian units, things were not going so fast the Allied had expected due in part to fanatical German resistance and in part to bad weather conditions.
